title: AMS 100 - Introduction to American Studies
description: An introduction to the history and key concepts of American Studies. Students explore major changes in American culture through critical reading and analysis of primary and secondary source material. Not open to students who have taken AMS 101.

title: AMS 101 - Introduction to American Studies (Honors)
description: Honors introduction to the history and key concepts of American Studies. Explores major changes in American culture through critical reading and analysis of primary and secondary sources. Open to Honors Program students or by permission.

title: AMS 110 - American Identities
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to individual and group identities over time, examining race, class, gender, sexuality, age, religion, and region from multiple perspectives.

title: AMS 171 - Religion in American Society
description: Broad introduction to religion in American culture, including major traditions and minority religions, and the relationship between religion, ethnicity, gender, and the state.

title: AMS 260 - Introduction to Latinx/Chicanx Studies

title: AMS 306 - Black Experience in the United States Since Emancipation

title: AMS 320 - Grounding U.S. Latinx Histories: Migration
description: Examines immigration, citizenship, and space through responses to Latinx migration, including issues of language, religion, security, and belonging.

title: AMS 321 - American Gun Culture
description: Explores the role of guns in U.S. society from sociological and cultural perspectives, addressing gun ownership, crime, gender, and public policy.

title: AMS 325 - Spanish for Heritage Learners
description: Comprehensive review of Spanish for heritage speakers, emphasizing cultural analysis and communication skills for advanced coursework.

title: AMS 332 - United States in Global Context
description: Examines U.S. influence abroad and global influences on the U.S., covering race, migration, imperialism, technology, and transnational organizations.

title: AMS 344 - Case Study in American Studies
description: In-depth examination of specific topics in American Studies, with rotating themes such as film and visual culture.

title: AMS 360 - Theory and Method
description: Introduction to theories and methods used in American Studies, emphasizing interdisciplinary analytical approaches.

title: AMS 365 - Men and Masculinities Today
description: Interdisciplinary exploration of masculinities in contemporary culture, including politics, media, race, gender, and LGBTQIA+ perspectives.

title: AMS 496 - Social Justice Perspectives and Experience
description: Experiential learning course focused on public and civic engagement related to social justice, integrating fieldwork with academic analysis.

title: AMS 551 - Research Project in American Studies
description: Independent research project under faculty supervision culminating in a substantial research paper or equivalent scholarly work.

title: AMS 552 - Public Service in American Studies
description: Independent public service project integrating experiential learning with academic research and reflection.

title: AMS 553 - Honors in American Studies
description: Honors-level independent study or research project in American Studies.

title: AMS 694 - Directed Readings
description: Supervised individual reading and study on a selected topic in American Studies.

title: AMS 696 - Studies in American Studies
description: Interdisciplinary study of selected aspects of the American experience; topics vary by semester.

title: AMS 700 - Introduction to Museum Exhibits
description: Introduction to exhibit management, design, and production, including conceptual development, installation, and evaluation.

title: AMS 799 - Museum Internship
description: Directed practical experience in museum research, collections, care, management, and public education.

title: AMS 803 - Research Methods in American Studies
description: Introduction to interdisciplinary research methods used in American Studies, focusing on assumptions, logic, and procedures.

title: AMS 896 - Examination Preparation (MA)
description: Independent preparation for the M.A. examination in American Studies.

title: AMS 900 - Teaching Seminar
description: Seminar on preparation, presentation, and evaluation of teaching in American Studies.

title: AMS 996 - Examination Preparation (PhD)
description: Independent preparation for doctoral comprehensive examinations.

title: AMS 997 - Directed Readings (Graduate)
description: Graduate-level directed reading in American Studies when no regular course offering is available.

title: AMS 998 - Seminar in American Studies
description: Graduate seminar with rotating topics; students are consulted in topic selection.

title: DANC 260 - Dance - Musical Theatre Dance
description: This course focuses on the dance and movement vocabulary uniquely associated with musical theatre productions, as well as a variety of popular dance styles from the 1920s to the present. Performance techniques for the stage are emphasized.

title: DANC 290 - Dance - Sophomore Review
description: The Sophomore Review of all majors in the BA program in Dance provides an assessment of student progress in the degree. Transfer students to the BA program participate in the year following their admission to KU. The review process consists of verification that students are making academic progress, including GPA review, self-evaluation, faculty evaluation, and participation in speedback sessions. Completion of the course is a prerequisite for enrollment in DANC 550 Senior Project.

title: DANC 313 - Dance - Modern/Contemporary III
description: Dance technique for intermediate/advanced dancers with precedents in the movement vocabularies of classical modernists and contemporary choreographers of dance. May be repeated for credit. Counts toward the B.A., B.F.A., and the Minor in dance requirements. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

title: DANC 315 - Dance - Jazz III
description: Dance technique for intermediate dancers based on elements of Latino, African, popular and classical jazz dance forms. May be repeated for variable credit. Prerequisite: DANC 105 or consent of instructor.

title: DANC 320 - Dance - University Dance Company
description: A dance repertory, performance and production class emphasizing the development of skills for performing and/or producing dance concerts. Admission by audition only. May be repeated for credit.

title: DANC 330 - Dance - Dance in Culture
description: Provides historical and cultural context for selected dance forms and their relationship to race, gender, sexuality, class, and nation through readings, master classes, performances, and film.

title: DANC 375 - Dance - Anatomy and Injury Prevention
description: Introduces neuromuscular and skeletal education using imagery (ideokinesis) with emphasis on body alignment, efficiency, and injury prevention.

title: DANC 411 - Dance - Ballet IV
description: Advanced level technique in classical and modern approaches to ballet. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

title: DANC 417 - Dance - Hip Hop II
description: Intermediate/advanced hip hop dance focusing on skills, combinations, choreography, isolations, and body control. Prerequisite: Hip Hop Fundamentals or permission of instructor.

title: DANC 498 - Dance - Directed Study in Dance
description: Investigation of a special topic or project in aesthetics, dance history, movement analysis, production, or a creative project. Maximum of six hours may count toward graduation. Prerequisite: At least seven hours of credit in dance courses.

title: DANC 540 - Dance - Field Experience in Dance Teaching
description: Teaching ballet, modern, or jazz dance technique with faculty supervision in academic or community programs. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

title: DANC 550 - Dance - Senior Project
description: In-depth research or choreography project involving complete development and presentation of a dance idea. Prerequisite: DANC 290 and permission of instructor.

title: DANC 580 - Dance - Special Topics in Dance
description: Study of current developments in dance emphasizing performance or research. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: Junior or senior standing or consent of instructor.

title: DANC 898 - Dance - Directed Study in Dance
description: Directed study in aesthetics, dance history, movement analysis, production, or advanced creative project. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

title: THR 105 - Theatre - Improvisation

title: THR 106 - Theatre - Acting I
description: Examines fundamental acting techniques including terminology, script analysis, and performance critique.

title: THR 120 - Theatre - Public Speaking as Performance
description: Integrates theatre practice with public speaking through speech assignments and performance-based exercises.

title: THR 201 - Theatre - Theatre Practicum II
description: One crew assignment in a University Theatre & Dance production. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: THR 101.

title: THR 206 - Theatre - Acting II
description: Study of roles and scenes emphasizing character analysis, rehearsal, and ensemble work. Prerequisite: THR 106.

title: THR 210 - Theatre - Musical Performance for Actor I

title: THR 213 - Theatre - Movement I: The Acting Instrument

title: THR 215 - Theatre - Approaching Design

title: THR 224 - Theatre - Lighting Production

title: THR 301 - Theatre - Theatre Practicum III

title: THR 302 - Theatre - Undergraduate Seminar in Theatre
description: Seminar on selected topics based on faculty expertise with discussion and projects.

title: THR 307 - Theatre - Undergraduate Theatre Internship
description: Supervised internship with approved theatre company or project. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

title: THR 308 - Theatre - Script Analysis

title: THR 310 - Theatre - Musical Performance for Actor II

title: THR 316 - Theatre - Beginning Scene Design

title: THR 318 - Theatre - Rendering for Design

title: THR 326 - Theatre - African Theatre and Drama

title: THR 380 - Theatre - Popular Culture

title: THR 401 - Theatre - Stage Management & Assistant Directing
description: Practical experience in stage management or assistant directing for University Theatre productions.

title: THR 406 - Theatre - Audition Techniques

title: THR 407 - Theatre - Advanced Acting Special Topic

title: THR 410 - Theatre - Musical Performance for Actor III

title: THR 801 - Theatre - Professional Development Seminar
description: Preparation for faculty careers including research, teaching, and service.

title: THR 815 - Theatre - Advanced Play Production

title: THR 819 - Theatre - Advanced MFA Production Seminar
description: Advanced continuation of MFA production seminar with complex design assignments.

title: THR 822 - Theatre - Scenography and Experimental Production
description: Experimental and mixed-media production design approaches.

title: THR 898 - Theatre - Investigation and Conference
description: Graduate-level independent research in theatre and performance studies.

title: THR 899 - Theatre - Master's Thesis
description: Individually directed thesis research for MA or MFA students.

title: THR 901 - Theatre - Theatre Seminar
description: Graduate seminar on historical, theoretical, or critical theatre issues.

title: JWSH 347 - Jewish Ethics
description: In this course we will explore the variety of ways that Judaism and Jewish people have approached ethics, both theoretically and practically. Our investigation will consider the evolution of approaches across time, and variations among different communities, as well as examining how the religious tradition has, at times, differed from actual practice among Jewish people. We will look at theological, philosophical, and sociological elements that inform Jewish ethics, as well as delving into specific issues in Jewish ethics, including autonomy vs. communal norms; business and labor practices; saving a life vs. taking a life; the treatment of animals; marriage and family matters; medical ethics; universalism vs. particularism, and more. Satisfies: Goal 5 Outcome 1 (AE51) , Arts and Humanities (AH)

title: JWSH 379 - Prophets and Profits

title: REL 145 - Jailbirds and Jayhawks
description: This course connects the history of Kansas to past and present freedom movements. Students explore the significance of the KU Jayhawk during 19th century anti-slavery struggles in Lawrence and “Bleeding Kansas.” Additionally, participants study broader 21st century resistance strategies captured by social media hashtags, public education campaigns, and collective action to re-galvanize a demand for abolition and the declaration that Black Lives Matter. A focal lens is to examine the role of multiracial, interreligious, and transglobal communities as a guide to advance a faith-based abolitionist movement that imagines a more just and equitable world. Students engage participatory research methods and apply theoretical learning to develop restorative and transformative justice strategies that advance the goals of abolition, including ending policing and prisons locally in the Kansas Metro area and globally. The key themes covered in this course are abolition and art, religion and resistance, gender and punishment, global mass/open-air prisons and walls, and building abolitionist sanctuaries. This class is an immersive and interactive experience that includes guest speakers, field trips, community organizing, and project-based learning oriented toward ethics and social justice. (Same as AAAS 145.)

title: REL 171 - Religion in American Society
description: A broad introduction to religion in American culture. This class emphasizes the well-established religions with large followings (viz. Judaism, Catholicism, Eastern Orthodoxy, and Protestantism). Some attention is also given to other religions active in America. Other topics covered include the relationship of church and state, religion in ethnic and racial minority groups, and women and religion. (Same as AMS 171.)

title: REL 190 - Special Topics in Religion
description: Topic and instructor to be announced in Schedule of Classes. May be offered by different instructors under different subtitles, and may be taken more than once if subject matter varies sufficiently.

title: REL 330 - Native American Religions
description: A survey of religious traditions among selected Native American peoples. Topics include religious freedom, ritual activity, cultural narrative (myth), kinship, healing practices, ecology, government relations, impact of colonization, impact of missionization, contact between cultures, and secularization.

title: REL 340 - Christianity and American Politics
description: This course examines the complex role of Christianity in American politics, with a special focus on the origins, rise, and ongoing impact of White Christian Nationalism. Although the course will focus on the rise of Christian nationalism in American politics, the origins of this ideology, which precede the founding of the United States, will also be examined. The course will include a look at early foundations of Christian Nationalism in medieval Catholicism, the Protestant Reformation, and the so-called Wars of Religion, as well as more recent developments in Christian political theology in the United States. By exploring the relationship between authoritarian political theology and right-wing politics, students will gain a more nuanced understanding of the religious and political forces at work in the United States today.

title: REL 343 - Christianity in Fantasy Literature
description: This course explores connections between Christianity and popular culture by examining four of the most prominent modern fantasy series: The Chronicles of Narnia by C.S. Lewis, The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R. Tolkien, Harry Potter by J.K. Rowling, and His Dark Materials by Philip Pullman. Through reading, discussing, and writing about these series, we will analyze the role played by Christianity in fantasy literature and discover how various theological themes are addressed in fantasy books. We will also reflect upon the difficulties inherent in determining what makes a text “religious” and explore how the author’s intentions, the audience’s interpretations, and other factors figure into this determination.

title: REL 373 - Supreme Court and Religious Issues in the United States
description: This course provides a historical study of the interpretation of the religion clauses of the First Amendment with special reference to the questions of establishment, the free exercise of religion, freedom of religious belief, worship, and action, and religion and the public schools. (Same as HIST 373.)

title: REL 379 - Prophets and Profits
description: The course will examine what religious traditions have had to say about controversies in economic ethics, focusing on how religious thinkers develop arguments on the basis of methods particular to their traditions. At the same time, it presents these traditions alongside secular approaches to economic ethics. Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism will be considered, as will liberalism, Marxism, feminism, and natural law theory. Topics include economic inequality, wealth accumulation, licit and illicit commerce, slavery, and profit. Attention will also be paid to the methodological challenges of the study of the topic, which necessarily brings together political economy, ethics, economic history, and hermeneutics. Students will work with a diverse array of primary sources, from ancient scriptures to modern thinkers. The ultimate goal will be to understand how it is possible for thinkers within the same religious tradition to take differing stances on economic ethics while considering themselves wholly grounded in tradition, depending on their relationships to the modern secular approaches we discuss. (Same as JWSH 379.)

title: REL 380 - Philosophical Issues in Religion
description: This course will consider, from a philosophical perspective, some of the problems in religion which arise in the development of "Natural Theology" broadly conceived. (Same as PHIL 350.)

title: REL 404 - Undergraduate Seminar in Religion
description: Topic, instructor, prerequisite and hours of credit to be announced in Schedule of Classes. Particular subject matter any given semester responding to student interest and taking advantage of special faculty competence. Class discussion, readings, and individual projects.

title: REL 405 - Directed Study in Religion
description: Investigation of a special topic or project selected by the student with advice, approval, and supervision of an instructor. Such study may take the form of directed reading or special research. Individual reports and conferences. May be repeated, with maximum cumulative credit of four hours. Course taken for one hour of credit may not be used to fulfill College distribution requirement. Prerequisite: One previous course in religious studies at the University of Kansas and permission of instructor.

title: REL 499 - Undergraduate Honors Research
description: Required for Departmental Honors. May be taken more than once; total credit not to exceed 6 hours. Prerequisite: Open only to candidates for degree with departmental honors and with consent of the student's research supervisor.

title: REL 500 - Readings in Non-English Religious Texts
description: This course provides directed readings for students in either primary or secondary texts related to religious studies utilizing material in languages other than English.
